title: General anesthesia
what: A deep sleep caused by medicine. You feel nothing and remember nothing. An anesthesiologist stays with you the whole time.
why: For surgery when you need full pain relief and must stay completely still.
duration: for the whole surgery; waking up usually takes 10 to 30 minutes
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and diabetes medicines. The doctor decides what to stop
Heart or lung disease, or sleep apnea
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia
If you smoke or drink alcohol

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and ask your questions.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 hours, and clear water up to 2 hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Your doctor will tell you which medicines to take in the morning. Do not stop anything on your own.

prepare.title: Before surgery
prepare.text: Take off jewelry, contact lenses, and dentures. Remove nail polish.

steps: A thin tube called an IV is put into a vein
In the operating room, sensors are stuck on your chest and finger
You breathe oxygen through a mask
The anesthesiologist gives the medicine, and you fall asleep within a minute
While you sleep, machines help you breathe and your heart is watched
After surgery, you wake up in the recovery room
feel: You fall asleep fast and do not remember the surgery
Your throat may feel scratchy from the breathing tube
Sometimes nausea. Tell the nurse and you will get medicine
after: You can eat and drink when the doctor says so
Do not drive for the first 24 hours
For the first 24 hours, do not make big decisions or drink alcohol
Weakness and fogginess usually pass in 1 to 2 days
red_flags: Trouble breathing or chest pain: call emergency services
Heavy vomiting that does not stop
Confusion that does not go away

faq.q: Can I wake up during anesthesia?
faq.a: This is very rare. The anesthesiologist checks how deeply you sleep on monitors the whole time.

faq.q: Why can't I eat before anesthesia?
faq.a: During sleep, food from the stomach can get into the lungs. An empty stomach protects you from this.

reminders.text: Surgery under anesthesia tomorrow. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
Have your last meal at the time your clinic said. Remove nail polish and jewelry.
